newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek archaeology watchdog slams Virgin hotel plan.
newsitem.headline: Greek archaeology watchdog slams Virgin hotel plan.

text.p: Greece's top archaeology watchdog Wednesday rejected plans by British entrepreneur Richard Branson's Virgin Group to build a hotel resort on the historic island of Hydra where no cars are allowed.
The powerful Central Archaeological Council (KAS) said in a decision issued Wednesday the hotel complex would alter the character of the Hydra village of Kaminia.
Although its role technically is only advisory, KAS decisions are never contradicted by the culture minister, who has the final say.

Branson's Virgin Hellas Hotel company envisioned a romantic complex of buildings, with winding paths, swimming pools and tennis courts on the island, which is a 90-minute hovercraft ride from the main Greek port of Piraeus.

Environmentalists and cultural preservation societies campained against the proposed 45,000 square-foot project, but islanders appeared before KAS to support the plan, saying it would create more than 100 permanent and 300 seasonal jobs.

"The island's 2,600 remaining residents are distressed at the decision. They feel the state wants to turn the island into a deserted archaeological site," Hydra mayor Constantine Anastopoulos was quoted as saying by the semi-official Athens News Agency.
Kaminia, a small village west of Hydra's port town can only be reached by mule path. It is a popular vacation spot for Greeks.
KAS said it would consider a new proposal for a much smaller hotel complex within the perimeter of the village, provided it did not include new roads, swimming pools, or sports facilities.
